assessments.summary: The analytic entropy argument establishes that receiver-skew symmetry gives M_T=L_{1/2,T}; conditional coordinate independence then makes the satellite terms additive and bounds the common terms by coordinate sums, yielding an upper bound nM_T. Independent epsilon-optimal one-letter copies give the reverse bound without requiring attainment. For arbitrary tuple laws over the product channel, direct entropy expansion establishes the stated total-correlation residual identity and makes positivity of the residual—and hence inequality (13)—necessary for any strict gain.
scopeQualifications: The theorem applies to finite receiver-skew two-receiver broadcast channels and to the specified conditional-product factorization with a common W that may induce unconditional coordinate correlation.
A strict-gain law must fail the conditional-product factorization for every exact chosen coordinate-packet decomposition to which the theorem applies.
For arbitrary tuple laws, the residual ledger and correlation-balance condition are relative to the chosen aggregate coordinate decomposition; they are noncanonical.
Inequality (13) is only a necessary condition for strict gain, not a sufficient condition.
Constant padding supplies a tuple representation, but does not make the ledger canonical or necessarily useful for pruning.
The result does not establish unrestricted Marton additivity, binary-input tightness, a capacity bound, or the exact half-skew BSSC capacity.
evidenceIssues: The reported fixed-seed floating-point computations test only finitely many examples and do not certify the universal theorem, arbitrary alphabets, or an 'exact ledger'; this is nonfatal because the analytic entropy proof independently establishes the claims.
